question: Is Westpac's targeted FY26 productivity enough to restore positive jaws, or is it mainly an offset to continuing wage, banker and UNITE investment pressure? Ground the judgment in the FY25 expense bridge, the investment-spend mix and the disclosed duration/expensing profile of UNITE.
answer:
**Direct answer.** On WBC's own FY25 disclosure (no FY26 document exists in this corpus), the >$500m targeted FY26 productivity looks like an **offset, not a jaws-restorer**. It is only ~$100m more than the $402m of productivity already delivered in FY25 — while the same FY25 bridge shows $1,101m of gross upward pressure — and it must absorb a 3–4% EBA rise, a superannuation increase, continued banker hiring and a UNITE step-up to $850–950m with ~75% expensed. Westpac gives no FY26 income or jaws guidance, so positive jaws cannot be confirmed either way from these documents.

**FY25 expense bridge (pack p27, FY25 vs FY24, $m):** 10,944 → 11,916 (+9%). Up: staff costs +397, technology +146, volume and other +199, investments +359, Fit for Growth restructuring +273; down: productivity −402 (ev-1, ev-22). Productivity therefore recovered only ~37% of the $1,101m gross non-restructuring pressure. Annotations attribute staff costs to "Salary and EBA increases", "Superannuation increase", "Investment in bankers" (ev-2/3/4) and investments to "UNITE investment $399m" and "Amortisation up $106m" (ev-8, ev-9). Momentum was worse in 2H25: productivity −249 against +496 of gross pressure plus the $273m charge (ev-39).

**Jaws in FY25 were sharply negative:** revenue +3% vs expenses +9% (+6% ex-restructuring), pre-provision profit −3% (ev-23); expense-to-income ex Notable Items 53.0% from 50.3% (ev-30). Staff expenses +7% to $6,326m "mainly due to wage growth, UNITE and the investment in bankers", with average FTE +1% as UNITE/banker hiring "more than offsetting reductions from productivity initiatives" (ev-31). Technology +13% to $3,136m (ev-28).

**Investment mix / UNITE profile.** FY25 investment $1,918m (+9%): UNITE 660 (34%), growth & productivity 563, risk & regulatory 695 (−34%) (ev-15, ev-25). Expensed share rose 4ppts to 60%; expensed dollars $1,159m vs $992m (ev-24, ev-25). UNITE FY25 was 74% expensed (ev-26; the pack prints 76%, ev-20 — a disclosure inconsistency). FY26: investment ~$2bn total, UNITE $850–950m at ~75% expensed, plan "extends into FY29", c.40% of total investment spend in FY27–FY28, lower spend FY29, c.1,600-person delivery team (ev-14, ev-17, ev-18, ev-19); amortisation growth to "moderate" from $995m (ev-13, ev-14). Cumulative UNITE spend $807m Oct-23 to Sep-25 against a ~40%-of-investment FY25–1H29 budget (ev-33, ev-35).

**Not settled:** no FY26 revenue/jaws/expense-growth guidance; no dollar sizing of FY26 EBA, super or banker costs; no FY26 productivity phasing or Fit for Growth benefit schedule.</answer>

limitations: The corpus holds no WBC document for FY26; this answer was researched in FY25 instead.
The corpus contains no WBC FY26 document; all figures are FY25 (or FY24 comparatives) and all FY26 items are targets/guidance, not outcomes.
Westpac publishes no FY26 revenue, expense-growth or jaws guidance, so whether jaws turn positive cannot be established from these documents.
The >$500m FY26 productivity target is not broken down by phasing, business or cost line, and no Fit for Growth benefit schedule or gross-vs-net definition is disclosed.
FY26 EBA (3–4%), superannuation and banker-investment costs are not quantified in dollars, so the comparison against >$500m of productivity cannot be closed arithmetically from printed figures.
Comparisons of the $402m FY25 productivity bar with the >$500m FY26 target assume a like-for-like definition, which the pages do not state.
The two documents disagree on the FY25 UNITE expensed share (74% in the results announcement vs 76% in the investor pack); the results announcement ranks higher under the source hierarchy.
UNITE initiative cost/benefit figures on pack p52 are estimates that were revised down between May-25 and Nov-25, and were not used to size FY26 benefits.
